key_insight: Embedding known physics in deep generative models does not by itself ensure identifiability; the paper presents meta-learning formulations with theoretical identifiability guarantees.
engineering_relevance: Identifiable hybrid models can make inferred physical parameters more trustworthy when combining mechanistic equations with neural generative components.
method: Analyze identifiability when physical and neural parameters are inferred jointly.
Construct meta-learning formulations of hybrid deep generative models.
Compare meta-formulations with existing hybrid models using unconditional priors.
evidence_signal: Synthetic and real-data benchmarks provide strong empirical evidence of non-identifiability in existing unconditional-prior models and identifiability in the proposed meta-formulations.
watch_item: Check the theorem assumptions and meta-learning data requirements before applying the identifiability guarantees to a new engineering system.
paper_title: On the Identifiability of Hybrid Deep Generative Models: Meta-Learning as a Solution
